notes: Keen Roof is one of the most popular hard boulder problems in the peak district, and in the UK as a whole, largely due to it's roadside location and high number of ascents meaning beta is easy to come by.

A classic boulder problem first climbed by Bernd Zangerl in 2002. The problem follows an overhanging rising crack with a challenging mix of crimps, slopers, and shoulder moves. Known for its technical demands and aesthetic line, it has become a popular test piece.
Alex Megos :
7b in to 7B with a kneebar rest, followed by an 8a+ headwall.
Originally considered 8B+/C, the crux pinch broke off around November 2009 and it is now considered 8C.
Originally put up at 8B+ but is now considered 8C and a contender for the world's first 8C boulder.

Action Directe is a legendary sport route in the Waldkopf area of the Frankenjura in Germany. It was first climbed by Wolfgang Güllich in 1991 who suggested a UIAA grade of XI (roughly 8c+/9a). It has since settled at 9a making it one of the first climbs at the grade in the world.

climb_name: To Bolt or Not to Be
notes: Among the most famous routes in the world, this wall of relentless edges played a seminal role in the consolidation of Sport Climbing being announced as the first 5.14a in North America.
A classic Johnny Dawes test piece. A hard move gains entry to the groove where easier climbing awaits before a terrifying finale.
A School Room classic, set by the prime Malcolm Smith
A long standing project of Mark Leach's . Unfortunately after working out the extension he was unable to repeat Mecca so the first ascent had to wait for Steve McClure .
A Peak District test piece, the soaring arête was so named because, while working the line, Jerry Moffatt proclaimed:
Kilnsey's first 8c. In 2024 a hold came off on the upper section making the route a little harder.
An old project from Chris Sharma and Dave Graham , features in dosage (vol 4?)

Immortalised in the 1994 film One Summer , Superman was one of the hardest problems around at the time of its first ascent, c.1989. The problem is somewhat eliminate; an easier version using all the holds is known as Superwoman.
Estado Crítico is notable for being the first ever 9a to be onsighted after Alex Megos climbed it in March 2012.

Bolted and named by Céüse pioneer and Alpine legend Jean-Christophe Lafaille in 1988, Arnaud Petit climbed the pitch to a half-height anchor in 1996 at a grade of 8c+. Chris Sharma climbed the the full pitch in 2001, after working it on-and-off for a few years and taking over 30 falls from the crux. In keeping with his style at the time, he did not grade the route [4], but it became widely credited as the first 9a+ in the world for a period; Open Air from 1996 was later upgraded to 9a+ to take that title.
The naming is somewhat confusing as first ascentionis Giuliano Cameroni has used it to refer to both the stand and the low. This is the stand start.
Originally 8A, upgraded to 8A+ after holds were chipped off in June 2001.

Sleepwalker is a boulder problem in Red Rocks in the USA. Nalle Hukkataival first cleaned and tried the line, and was then joined by Jimmy Webb and Daniel Woods in trying it. Jimmy Webb made the first ascent, shortly followed by Daniel Woods. After a prolonged battle with skin and conditions Nalle was able to make the third ascent.
Originally climbed as an easier variation of Salathé Wall , avoiding the hard crack pitches on the headwall, Freerider is now one of the most popular free routes on the main face of El Capitan .
Previously a Dave Graham project before Daniel Woods made the first ascent in 2007. In 2015 Adam Ondra flashed the problem, a wild piece of climbing.
Originally given 8C but due to a chipped hold, some soft rock and vigorous brushing holds have changed and it is now more like 8B/+.

First climbed to an intermediate lower off ( La Rambla (L1) (8c+)) by Alex Huber in 1994, it was then extended to the current lower off by Ramón Julián Puigblanque in 2003 for which he suggested 9a+, while also suggesting Alex's original line was likely harder than the 8c+ that was originally suggested.

The prow at Black Rocks is one of the most impressive and uncompromising features on gritstone and for decades was regarded as a Last Great Problem. Attention in the late ‘80s and early ‘90s focused on the prow’s left arête, with climbing said to be around 8b.
Originally climbed from a slightly higher start and called Ummagumma , Klem Loskot added the lower start a week later.

Originally given 9a, consensus is around 8c/+.
Ted Kingsnorth on hold deterioration:
Very morpho. 8B if you are tall enough to span the first move, otherwise you have to dyno which is worth 8B+.
A defining route of the Ron Fawcett era, and one of the most prized onsights in the UK. The route tackles a tasty crackline, followed by a fruity runout up the Vector headwall.
First climbed by Mark Leach after one of the most legendary sieges on Yorkshire limestone.
Originally given E8.
The first 8c+ in Norway.
First 9a route in Norway.
Around 2019 some pebbles broke on the crux holds making the problem slightly harder.
Previously called the Black 90 project a reference to Jade which was called the Green 45 project before it was climbed.
Around 8a+ to 8b difficulty wise, protected by pegs and small wires. The in-situ gear has changed since the first ascent:

A psychological breakthrough hailed at the time as one of the most difficult routes in the UK. Whilst clearly a step-up from the Brown - Whillans era, with the benefit of hindsight, there were already a number of harder routes by the time of its first ascent. Nonetheless it possessed a considerable cachet until attaining trade-route status by the mid-1980s.
The Nose is one of the most monumental and iconic rock climbs in the world, taking the most prominent line up the middle of El Capitan .

One of the most compelling single pitch lines out there, Divided Years tackles a 55m prow at Buzzard's Roost in the Mournes. It was the first route to be given E10 in the world in 1994, and was said to feature 8c climbing. It now rates E9, with climbing around 8a+.
5D in the Japanese bouldering grading system.
The first 8c+ in the USA.
One of the eight ‘last great problem’ projects listed in the Derwent Grit guide. [1]
Originally put up as 8B+, the consensus seems to have shifted to 8B.
A new sequence with kneebars has significantly reduced the difficulty compared to the original sequence.
The 'Mona Lisa of bouldering', according to Niccolò Ceria , this stunning arête is one of the quintessential problems of Fontainebleau.
Alex Megos 's contribution to the legendary School 50. A modern classic.
Named after John Allen , a prolific force in the Peak District, who sadly died shortly before the first ascent.

Originally climbed with a desperate feet low sequence (~8B), this was subsequently improved slightly with a toe on the rail (abely demonstrated by Ben Moon in Hard Grit) before some heel hooking technique was applied which lowered the grade to 7C.
Lou Ferrino in to Trigger Cut .

The first proposed 8C, it was later downgraded to 8B+ when Dave Graham found a heel hook. There were also suggestions of hold improvement. Around November 2009 the crux pinch broke off making the problem harder. Dreamtime is now considered 8C again.
Generally considered to be 8c+/9a.
Climber :
Originally given 8C+ but later a downgrade to 8C was suggested by the FA Paul Robinson .

Allegedly conceptualised by John Yablonski whilst under the influence of LSD. Named after the Jimi Hendrix song as it was considered as unlikely as lightning striking at midnight and for the lightning bolt shaped hold.

Initially given 9a which would have made Adam Ondra's 2012 ascent the first onsight of the grade. However Adam felt the route was more 8c+ and Daniel Woods , who flashed the route on the same day, agreed.
Considered to be one of the first 8B+s in the world.
Jerry Moffatt 's hardest and final route at Raven Tor , blasting up a line of punishing crimps. Ben Moon , who repeated the route aged 52:
Golden Gate climbs the first 21 pitches of Salathe/Freerider then ~9 new pitches links it into the last 7 pitches of El Corazon.
Originally a project of Mark Leach's before Steve McClure took up the reins and made the first ascent.
5.13c/8b, and likely E9, if the headwall is climbed in a single pitch.

Originally climbed without pads at E8. As with other lines on this bloc it utilises a large carved runnel to get established on the base of the slab. The runnel is believed to be a historical 'drip edge detail' for a dwelling or shelter that once stood under the roof.
The difficulty is pretty dependent on height. Taller climbers can use a low foothold which makes it substantially easier. [1]
One of the first 8Bs in the world, though improvements to the sequence have led many to suggest 8A+ is more appropriate.
The first 14b in America.

Originally climbed with a sika'd hold by Nic Sellars in 1992 and named 'Justified and Ancient', a song by The KLF. Then claimed as Yorkshire's first 8c after being reclimbed by Tony Mitchell without the sika'd hold. Subsequently an easier method looping out right was discovered, resulting in the route settling at 8b+
Ben Moon :
Generally considered to be 9a/+.
The crux first move is 8B+ on it's own, with a tricky ~8Aish sequence still to do after you stick the start.
Mt. Kasagiyama, Ena, Gifu, Japan
Previously a project of Bernd Zangerl's .

Hubble is a route at Raven Tor in the UK's Peak District. Ben Moon made the first ascent of the full line in 1990 suggesting a grade of 8c+, making it the hardest route in the world at the time. It is now considered closer to 9a, making it both the first 8c+ and the first 9a!
One of the first 9as established in the USA.
Considered the hardest of the 8B trio, with some today considering it 8B+. This didnt see a repeat for nearly 20 years until Alex Megos repeated it in 2016
One of the first 8b+s in the world. Possibly slightly easier now than for Güllich and Glowacz since the construction of the birdbath hold subsequent to their ascents.
Originally thought to be 8B/+. A 'crucial' side pull broke after the first ascent but it was later re-climbed without the side pull.
Around 2018 the crux hold was chipped making the problem slightly easier. [1]
Named after Dál Riata, a Gaelic kingdom that spanned the western coast of Scotland and north-eastern Ireland.
So-named because it was said it would never go free.

climb_name: Once Upon a Time in the Southwest
notes: Johnny Dawes likely abseiled the line in 1989. Nick White writing in Mountain 129:
A more direct start to Power of Now avoiding some reachy moves on the original.
Overhanging groove right of Minaret (E8).

A groundbreaking route, taking on the impressive central crack line up the centre of Dumbarton Rock . Originally graded E7 when first climbed by Dave 'Cubby' Cuthbertson in 1983, it was upgraded to E8 by Dave MacLeod in 2000.
A stunning coastal slab adventure whose immense proportions are perhaps only exceeded by the size of the grading controversy that accompanied its first ascent.

The first 8A in the forest, climbed by Jacky Godoffe after six months of effort.
85m long, 200+ moves, 24 quickdraws and 1hr+ to climb it!
Originally given 8C, now considered 8B+.

Perhaps the most celebrated and revered route in the UK, Johnny Dawes ' ascent in 1986 gave the country its first E9. Although only around 7b/+ to top rope, the route is exceptionally bold, running it out way above bodyweight-only RPs in suspect placements. A fall from the precarious crux at around 40m would likely end on the ground.
From the start of Ben's Roof climb direct into Keen Roof, do not go to the kneebar.

While working the problem Charles Albert found a more direct alternative sequence. His sequence is reliant on using a pocket with your toe, so it is generally considered as a separate problem Le Pied à Coulisse (Direct) .
Originally 8B+, a contender for the first of the grade in the Forest. After a hold broke it became 8B.

One of the first sport routes in the UK to be climbed in 'red point' style, where the moves were practised before the final ascent. Prior to this routes were more typically climbed onsight or in yoyo style where pre-practicing the moves wasn't allowed.
A left hand finish to Pegasus .
~8a+ on ok-ish gear.
Originally given 8c/+ repeat ascenionists then suggested 8c+. Around 2018/2019 some holds broke on the crux and it is now considered more 9a.
One of the most famous routes in the dolomites.
A historic gritstone king line, which was solved well ahead of its time by Jonny Woodward in 1982, in non-sticky boots.
The board climb, set  as a replica/trainer for lucid dreaming on the 2016 Moon Board
Perhaps the most famous and celebrated trad route in Britain, taking on the obvious challenge of the open-book corner of Dinas Cromlech .
Formerly an aid route.
First climbed as an aid route in the 90s
The first 9a in France.
Links The Wheel of Wolvo in to We Can Build You .
First 8b route in Norway.
The first 8c+ in America established by an American, the soon to be famous Chris Sharma . Jim Thornburg writing in Climbing magazine #168:

Named after Yosemite climbing pioneer John Salathé . After fixing to the Heart Ledges, the remainder of the route was climbed on-sight. This was a notable improvement in style over the multi-season siege of The Nose (A2)
A Mizugaki testpiece on the historic Kotei Iwa boulder.
Chris Sharma's original line, and world famous testpiece. Start sitting on the right facing fin, then wrestle your way up and right through the sick, sloping features.
First ascentionist Daniel Woods :

Ed Drummond climbed the first pitch at a slightly lower level than the current line, top-roping it first, placing a bolt, pitons and using skyhooks (a total of 5 points of aid) on the 8th July 1973. This was omitted from the 1976 guide on ethical grounds although other routes of the time had employed similar amounts of aid.

Right hand line to Steppenwolf (8B)

The first 9A boulder problem in the world. Nalle Hukkataival made the first ascent in October 2016 and the problem received significant attention from many of the strongest boulderers in the world ( Toru Nakajima , Shawn Raboutou and Aidan Roberts to name a few) before Will Bosi made the second ascent in April 2023.

Originally climbed by pinching the right hand starting hold and making a powerful move to the first crimp and given 8B with this sequence. Subsequently the beta has improved and now involves guppying the starting right hand hold and using a left heel to make the first move static.
Goes left from a similar start to From the Dirt Grows the Flowers .
A pioneering route up Trango's Nameless Tower, encompassing hard free and mixed climbing at 6000m.
Named after the late Ed Stone . [1]

First climbed by Marc le Menestrel in 1996 before a hold broke. Re-ascended by Nalle Hukkataival in 2015 via a minor variation in line, finishing slightly right. Original line re-ascended by Charles Albert in 2016.
Does the start of Noia before linking in to the hard end section of Anaconda via some difficult moves.
The hardest route on Dinas Cromlech . 8a climbing with spicy gear.
The name comes from the infamous chipped pockets that make the problem possible.
Initially given 8B.
Originally graded 12a (~7a+) in the mid-80s it went down to 11d after a block at the end of the route broke off leaving a good edge .
John Dunne :

Originally climbed with no pads and a single ball nut for protection. James gave it E10, believing any fall would involve hitting the ground. Subsequent ascents tested the ball nut (above pads) and found it to be better than expected with the ball nut holding around 20 falls. Based on this, grades around E7 to E8 were suggested.
Originally climbed as a trad route at ~E7.
Start as for Gourmandise and finish as for Le Dernier Fléau .
First top-roped by Johnny Dawes in 1989, the name refers to the time that he was born.
The first E9 in Scotland. Repeats have taken a slight variation through a line of least resistance, rather than MacLeod's original. [1]

Akira is a route with a complicated history and a degree of controversy, largely because first ascentionist Fred Rouhling suggested a grade of 9b, at a time when 9a was the cutting edge and no routes had been proposed at 9a+ (though some routes from the era have subsequently been upgraded to 9a+, for example Mutation at Raven Tor ). Subsequent ascentionists have suggested 9a is more appropriate. To complicate things even further, the repeat ascentionists chose not use kneebars but suggested that using them would lower the grade further.
First discovered by Dave Graham it was a project for a long time before Shawn Raboutou made the first ascent.
Before Kevin Jorgeson made the first ascent George Ulrich , starting off a ladder, climbed the highball section but was unable to do the hard start.
Originally climbed without knee bars and given 8C, now considered to be 8B.
A Steve Wunsch project before Barber's impressive nuts-only protected onsight ascent.
Iwagoya Boulder, Horai, Aichi, Japan
FRCC Scawfell Guide 1924:
The first 9a+ in Germany.
After making the first ascent with 2 pegs in place Dave Birkett placed a bolt just above the pegs. This was quickly chopped.
El Corazón takes features originally aid climbed by Flight of the Albatross, Heart Route and Son of Heart linked by some new climbing. The name means The Heart in Spanish.
The leaning wall to the right of Launch Pad . The line had been a longstanding project.
Reverses Master Key before climbing Guest List .
Crown jewel of the somewhat obscure crag of Valsaín, Segovia, next to the river conditions are tricky as it is wet most of the winter. Sit start, it is also done from a stand as an 8A, same name.
This boulder was originally named "Ill Trill", however, the Magic Wood guidebook has it incorrectly listed as "Ill Thrill" and most other sources have followed suit.
Originally given 8c but upgraded following repeats. Jerry Moffatt named the route in memory of his brother, who loved Liquidambar trees.
8c/+ on trad gear. The breakdown is roughly an 8A boulder in to 8b route in to 7C boulder. Footholds, some glue-reinforced, have broken since the first ascent.

Named after Jerry Moffatt who decked from the upper reaches of the route on a previous attempt at the FA. Miraculously he survived relatively unscathed, using up one of his nine lives. Having completed all the hard, dangerous climbing and found a good runner he was stumped by the dirty top section so decided to lower off the runner. The runner failed and he landed flat on his back and was knocked unconscious, but miraculously awoke unscathed.

Tried extensively by Ben Moon . Despite coming close around 1995 was unable to finish the route due to a combination of poor conditions and injury. Steve McClure's successful ascent in July 2000 represented a passing of the torch, with him taking on the mantle as the UK's pre-eminent sport climber by finishing off Ben's old project.
A very long boulder problem. Around 8c+ to 9a as a sport route depending on how many knee bars you find.
Free version of the Muir Wall with some variations in line.
Eneko Pou :

Originally led but now typically done above a big pile of mats at about 7C+. On the first ascent Jerry Moffatt took a fairly direct line at the top, whereas people typically traverse round to the right before topping out when climbing the line above pads.
Initial attempts at a sit start to Sleepwalker were coming in from the left, but after shifting a boulder out of the way a line coming in from the right was made possible.

Rhapsody is a trad route at Dumbarton Rock in Scotland first climbed by Dave MacLeod in 2006. It was the hardest trad route in the world at the time and maintains a substantial reputation, featuring 8c+ climbing, and potential for huge falls onto tiny gear from the 8A crux at the top of the route.
So named because first ascentionist Dave Graham was recovering from a nasty hand injury when he established the problem.

The route had previously been climbed in two parts: the bottom half as One Step Beyond Direct by Ron Fawcett , and the top as Homeward Bound by Peter Beal . Johnny combined the two to complete the natural line up the middle of the wall.
One of the first 8as in the UK. The name is a play on the book Testament of Youth and the fact Ben Moon was a mere 18 years old when he made the first ascent.
Currently (2023) the hardest first ascent by a woman in the UK after Karin Magog made the first ascent in 2006.
A very short route or a highball boulder with a bit of a funky landing. When climbed as a route both the bolts on the route are usually pre-clipped.
Dan Varian :
Equipped by Ernst Hunsicker in 1987 and one of the first routes graded 8c when Wolfgang Güllich made the first ascent in the same year.
Some say 8c+/9a.
Finish without the rib.
As for Bélial but finishing right with the rib.

Bellavista pushed multi-pitch climbing in the Dolomites to new levels of difficulty via some wildly overhanging territory. The route tackles the enormous roofs of Cime Ovest overhanging some 60m over its 283m length. Lead protection comes primarily from pegs and some trad gear. Alexander Huber spent 5 weeks working the route prior to making the first ascent, describing it as “by far the wildest route on an alpine face”. [2]

First bolted by Ethan Pringle who quickly abandoned it as too hard for him. It took Alex Megos a lot of effort over multiple years to finally make the first ascent. Initially proposed at 9c it later settled at 9b+ after a relatively quick repeat by Stefano Ghisolfi .
A 1988 test piece, the line and method is quite strict, with many an aspirant taking the tick, then finding they have actually done the easier variant Fucking Golden .
Named after a large fish-shaped feature in the middle of the problem.

The route has suffered various breaks. It started off at 8c, then was around 8b+ when Dave Macleod made his solo ascent in 2008 but had gone back up to 8c by the time Jorge Díaz-Rullo made his solo ascent in 2021.
The third route to be free climbed on El Capitan , after Salathé Wall and The Nose .
The first 8C in Spain.
[1] https://touchstoneclimbing.com/hasta-la-vista-with-ethan-pringle/

Originally a project of Dave Graham's from 2004. Dave gave up on the project before Giuliano Cameroni established first the stand and then the sit. Dave then returned to climb both the stand and the sit.
A link of Maginot Line and Terminator .
Named after the H P Lovecraft short story.
12 of the pitches are 7c+/5.13 or harder including two 8b+/5.14a. Due to its sustained nature it may be the second-hardest free wall on El Capitan (2025).
Jerry Moffatt 's solution to the Last Great Problem on Clogwyn Du'r Arddu 's Great Wall. It has been the scene of some the most stomach-turning epics in British climbing.
Originally graded as a tentative 8C+ before settling at 8B+.
Originally graded 5.13b, the route is currently 5.12b; the route continues to be a popular aid route, which has enlarged cracks and holds in the soft sandstone.
The first 5.11 in Yosemite.
In Welsh mythology Olwen is the goddess of the sun.
The first 8B in Wales.

One of the hardest at the time.
Norway
The route lost a 'crucial' pebble in the late '90s and didn't see further ascents until 2008.
The first 14a/8b+ established by an American ( Scott Franklin ) in the US. There is debate about the grade with some suggesting 8b (or 13d).
[1] https://gripped.com/news/lucas-uchida-makes-first-ascent-of-wild-squamish-v14/
To the right of Trieste . 8B into two hard, low percentage moves.
Originally given E8, the landing has since been substantially improved to make for a more approachable 8A+.
Terremer starts at Diaphanous Sea and does the first 2 moves then moves left to meet up with Terre de Sienne .

...I don't have a preference. It's called The Direct Line, but it was known as the Platinum Wall before it was ever established, for the simple explanation that I was up there a long, long time. So, in the sense we don't get to choose our nicknames, mine being Platinum...
One of the hardest problems in the world at the time and a contender for the first 8A+.
A Johnny Dawes project which he was trying ground up before Robin Barker applied his considerable talents to the problem. 7C highballing to some gear in the break and a still-tricky finish.
The second 9a in the Frankenjura, after Action Directe .

climb_name: When Life Gives You Lemons Low

notes: The free version takes a different line for the first 5 pitches.
Ben Moon :
Although given E6 it is now typically done above a pile of pads at a highball ~7A. The pad-less version is a scary prospect!
Named after a big hold in the middle of the problem.
An adventurous Pen Llŷn sandbag whose reputation far exceeds its modest grade.
One of the hardest boulders in Sogn.
Bon Voyage is an extremely hard trad route in Annot , France. It starts up Le Voyage before breaking left across poor pockets to an arete.

Initially 8C+ was suggested and the first few repeats seemed to agree with this. In 2023 Katie Lamb climbed the problem, which would have made her the first woman to climb 8C+, but subsequent ascentionists have suggested that 8C is more appropriate and Daniel Woods (who made the first ascent) has retrospectively adjusted his opinion to 8C.

Conveniently situated near the graveyard of the Morewenstow Church, Henna is the highest precipice on the Culm coast and the most frightening.  The only route up the main cliff might well be available when other crags hereabouts become too overcrowded. A huge boulder lies ominously beneath the central fault-line.  Terrordactyls, ice-screws, stakes and a strong belief in one’s immortality are the main requirements for an ascent. After pitch 2 retreat would be at best extremely difficult or at worst terminally easy. [1]
the name spotted on the destination board of a bus in Chester as they returned home which fitted well with the tone of the adjacent routes Cenotaph Corner and Ivy Sepulchre.
A 40m long off-width roof crack in the White Rim : an outrageous adventure into horizontal suffering, and the hardest off-width in the world at the time of the first ascent.
The first 9b+ in the world.
An easier variation has become popular, where you climb to a slightly higher spike on Fay .

A hard direct start to Braille Trail which lands you on the 'rest' with no gear, meaning the precarious upper slab is unprotected. The name is from a geography module Pete Whittaker was studying in school at the time he made the first ascent.
Bolted in 2006 by Ally Smith and Freddy Mead they then tried the route in 2007 before abandoning it. Freddy then came back 16 years later and finished off the line!
A contender for the first 8C+.
Harder Faster is the harder, scarier direct finish to Gaia .
Stand start 8A+
A contender for the world's first 8C+ boulder.
A link up combining the lower part of Joe Blau with the upper part of La Marroncita .
The original line stepped left out of the gutter before making a couple of slab moves to the arete. An easier pop-to-the-top straight from the gutter was later discovered.

One of the hardest slab problems in the world. The impeccably smooth Fukano Slab ("impossible slab") was one of the last great problems in Ogawayama bouldering, initially solved by Toshimichi Kusano 's Zutsu (8B), which starts centrally and traverses off left.

Le Bombé Bleu was a legendary project bolted by Marc Le Menestrel in 1991. In an era when chipping was prolific Marc wanted to keep the route unchipped, as a challenge for future generatons, and in return opened the project up for all to try. In 2026 Erwan Legrand , son of François Legrand , made the first ascent in a relatively quick 15 sessions.
Jonas Winter :
A counter line to Impact Day . About 8b+ with a very spicy runout.
One of the most iconic and compelling highballs in the world. Initially graded 8C, but now considered a contender for the world's first 8C+ boulder.
A superb effort, free climbing the majority of the Longhope Route (A2), tackled ground-up by John Arran and Dave Turnbull ], taking in some of the most adventurous climbing in the UK.

Bolted by Kim Carrigan in 1982 this route was ahead of its time ( Kanal im Rücken , typically considered the first 8b in the world, was only climbed in 1984). Carrigan came tantalizingly close to making the first ascent but it had to wait for Stefan Glowcaz to finish it off .

A project of Ron Kauk's before he suffered an injury which stopped him trying the line. Beth Rodden then invested substantial time and energy in to the line before making the first ascent in 2008. The line then waited an incredible 10 years before receiving a second ascent from Carlo Traversi .
Norwegian grade 9-. Named in memory of Robert Caspersen's brother who died while abseiling Presten .
The peak of old school, vert micro crimping? One of the hardest problems in the UK when it was established and rarely repeated to this day.
Adam originally suggested 9b/+ but Sébastien Bouin suggested a rare upgrade after his ascent.
8b/+ depending on how well you fit the thin hands section.
The first 8c+ in Italy.
Initially Ramón Julián Puigblanque climbed the full line, then at a later date an intermediate lower off was added that avoided the upper 8b+ section, as this is frequently wet.
Grade might have changed sightly with holds changing over time.
Four new pitches 8b+, 8c, 6c, 6c linking Bellavista (E10)  with the Cassin Route (E5)
12 moves
First climbed by Jerry Moffatt after a long layoff, during which he got into fast motorbikes. A powerband on a bike is the specific RPM range where an engine produces its maximum torque and power.
In early 2025 the large flake which makes up the start of the problem broke off. [1]
Tried by Sébastien Bouin and Charles Albert before Alex Megos made the first ascent. Named because it's on the Face de Rat .

Originally proposed as '4-dan or harder' (4-dan equates to 8A+/8B), this 6m-tall king line is listed as 5-dan 8B+ on Rocktopo and v13/14 in repeater's videos. Either way, likely to be one of the hardest crack boulders in the world.
Named for a dislike of RockFax.
Trolldalen, Norway

A long standing project that saw a lot of attention before finally succumbing to Simon Lorenzi after 25 days of work.
An estimated 5.13b including a hard-to-grade horizontal dyno for his free ascent.
Links Evolution in to the end of Kaa'bah .
Extension to The Brute .

The original aid route was called The Bulge , but when Craig Smith made the first free ascent he renamed it Let Them Eat Jellybeans (because people were scratching around for lines at Malham Cove while he made the FA). However the original name stuck.

The first route to breach the south east face of El Capitan by the all-star team of Robbins , Pratt , Frost and Chouinard . After several exploratory attempts by Robbins with Glen Denny and Frost the ascent was accomplished in one push with no fixed ropes. This was the first time a route had been established in this style on El Capitan and in marked contrast to the extensive fixed ropes employed on the multi-month ascents of The Nose and Dihedral Wall. It was graded A5 and regarded as probably the hardest in the world of its genre at the time of ascent.

At the time of his ascent, Adam described it as the second hardest route he had ever done (behind Silence ). The route starts with a 25 move power endurance section, which is 9a+ by itself, into the crux of an existing 8b+ route. From there, a good undercling, a splits position, and a knee bar offer good resting opportunities before the crux boulder problem. The 8B+ boulder problem revolves around a crux shoulder move (8A+ one move) and a triple bump sequence after an intro 8A section. After the last hard move, a potentially heartbreaking 7A section followed by easy exit climbing takes it to the chains.
